# A loop html writes into a page's markup has its iterable worked out while
# the page is built. One that cannot be -- here a function that raises -- is
# refused at the loop. Written as it stood, its body came out once with its
# variable bound to nothing: an empty element, and a handler naming a variable
# nothing declared.
#
# A loop an override's body holds is reported at the node the program wrote,
# since the override's position is nothing the program can act on: menubar's
# entries, written under a `for` over the same function, are walked by the
# loop in html's own override.

! sngl generate --platform=html --out out own.sngl
stderr 'own.sngl:10:9: this loop is written into the page, and what it iterates cannot be worked out while the page is built'

! sngl generate --platform=html --out out override.sngl
stderr 'override.sngl:9:7: this loop is written into the page, and what it iterates cannot be worked out while the page is built'

-- own.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

func names() list<string> {
    error.raise("no names", "test")
    return ["File"]
}

ui.window {
    ui.vbox {
        for var n = names() {
            ui.text(value=n)
        }
    }
}
-- override.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

func names() list<string> {
    error.raise("no names", "test")
    return ["File"]
}

ui.window {
    ui.menubar {
        for var n = names() {
            ui.menuItem(label=n)
        }
    }
}
